clue.text: Canine's unhappy about handling: "Walk backwards!"

indicators.note: the sad word goes round, about, the handling word, which sits inside it

parts.note: unhappy means sad
handling, the way a thing is treated, is its usage

indicators.note: backwards tells us to read the word for walk from right to left

parts.note: to walk is to go

explanation.surface: A sorrowful dog's owner barks at it to back away while handling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backwards' looks like part of the command to the dog, but it turns GO into OG to finish the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dachshund is popularly nicknamed a sausage dog for its long body, so it is a breed of canine.

clue.text: Ham: a processed meat to preserve without its skin

indicators.note: processed meat has been worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the outer letters, the skin, are stripped from the word for preserve

parts.note: to preserve food, by salting or smoking, is to cure it

explanation.surface: Ham explained as cured meat, the rind taken off for keeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' turns MEAT into MATE; CURE loses its outside letters to leave UR.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is slang for a poor or non-professional performer, as in ham radio or ham actor: an unskilled hobbyist.

clue.text: Drug set-up might help reduce calling time

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine

indicators.note: in a down entry, up says the word for set is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to set down is to lay, past tense laid

explanation.surface: An arrangement for supplying narcotics is said to save time on phone calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LAID to give DIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone's quick-dial button stores a number so a call is placed with a single press, cutting the time spent placing it.

clue.text: Newspaper has 50% off Nintendo console screens

indicators.note: half of the paper's name is discarded, so only its first four letters are kept

parts.note: The Guardian is the British daily newspaper
the DS is a handheld games console made by Nintendo

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a half-price offer on a Nintendo gaming device.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen something is to shield it, and guards are protective shields, so both mean protects.

clue.text: Firm, top chef beginning to cook gluten? I can't stomach it

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: top means the head letter of the chef's name is taken off

parts.note: Delia Smith is a famous British television cook

indicators.note: beginning to picks only the opening letter of the word cook

explanation.surface: A company's head chef starts cooking, and a diner protests that gluten disagrees with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' here removes Delia's first letter rather than meaning best, leaving ELIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with the coeliac condition reacts to gluten and cannot digest it, so the clue's protest is what such a person says.

clue.text: Rejects old TUC assembly as extremely tedious

indicators.note: an assembly puts parts together in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, first and last, of tedious

explanation.surface: The old Trades Union Congress conference is dismissed as dreadfully boring.
explanation.walkthrough: The TUC is the Trades Union Congress, the UK federation of trade unions; 'assembly' looks like a meeting but rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Outcasts are people cast out by society, as rejects are those turned away.

clue.text: Slow left-arm — good over, but not maiden

indicators.note: but not tells us to remove the maiden letter from arm

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cricket report on a slow left-arm bowler whose good over still conceded runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored; slow left-arm is a style of spin bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a very slow, broad tempo.

clue.text: Wine Foreman is able to drink but ___ ?

definitions.text: Wine Foreman is able to drink but ___ ?

parts.words: Wine Foreman is able to drink but ___ ?
parts.note: George Foreman can drink, but Muhammad Ali, his famous rival, could not: drop the boxers' first names and the blank is filled by a Spanish wine's name

explanation.surface: A boxer may take alcohol, but his rival in the ring may not.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali, a Muslim, did not drink alcohol; Foreman fought him in the 1974 Rumble in the Jungle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicant is a sweet red wine from the Alicante region of Spain, filling the blank as a pun.

clue.text: Ulterior motives revealed here laterally?

parts.note: the grid's outer left and right columns spell two words for a timetable or diary, concealed at the sides

explanation.walkthrough: The left column spells SCHEDULE and the right CALENDAR, two kinds of agenda at the sides of the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret aims kept from others are ulterior motives, the hidden purposes behind an action.

clue.text: 100 + 1 + 10? A connected series

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100
A, like one, means a single thing
ten spelt out

explanation.surface: A sum of numbers is offered as an example of a chain of linked items.
explanation.definitionFit: A catena is a chain or linked succession of things, from the Latin for chain.

clue.text: Knitting pattern created by the first artisan?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the first

indicators.note: created means the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A design in knitwear was devised by the earliest craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Intarsia is a knitting technique in which blocks of coloured yarn form a picture or motif.

clue.text: Old flyer: "The start of rationing: no bread rolls"

indicators.note: the start of picks the first letter of rationing
rolls means the letters tumble over into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wartime rationing began with no bread rolls being allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolls' looks like bread rolls but tumbles NO BREAD into EDBARON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Baron, Manfred von Richthofen, was the German First World War flying ace.

clue.text: Ran and played the ball

definitions.meaning: to have ... a firm or team is to have led or run it
in football, to have struck the ball with the head

explanation.definitionFit: Headed means both was in charge of something and struck a football with the head.

clue.text: Crooked Democrat's in gaol with a criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters are bent out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A corrupt politician is locked up in prison along with a lawbreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal, putting the Democrat inside the gaol, but it is part of the fodder for 'criminal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal line slants or runs askew rather than straight, so it is crooked.

clue.text: Wise monarch's regularly unwise

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of unwise, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A sovereign's sage is, at times, quite foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise; 'Wise' is his surname, not wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernie Wise was the comedian partnered with Eric Morecambe, so the surname points to his first name.

clue.text: Start eating — it's served up

indicators.note: served up suggests a dish presented in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A diner is told to tuck in now the food has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To instigate something is to set it going or bring it about, to start it.

clue.text: Passed a drug around to deliver 8d

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: 8 sounds like ate, and d is the abbreviation for down

explanation.surface: Someone hands round a narcotic to supply the wine of another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '8d' looks like a cross-reference to the wine, but read as eight-d it gives ATE (sounding like eight) and D (down).
explanation.definitionFit: To have graduated is to have completed and passed a course of study.

clue.text: Hymn ends with one listener doing a somersault!

parts.note: to die is to end, so ends is dies
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: doing a somersault flips the word for listener upside down, reading it upwards

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A hymn finishes as a lone member of the audience turns head over heels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing a somersault' turns EAR into RAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies Irae, day of wrath, is the Latin hymn sung in the Requiem Mass.

clue.text: Heather's after raunchy flip-flops, or maybe flats

indicators.note: after places the heather word behind the other piece
flip-flops means the word for raunchy turns over, read backwards

parts.note: raunchy means lewd
ling is another name for heather; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather follows some risqué beach sandals, perhaps flat ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flip-flops' looks like footwear but reverses LEWD to DWEL; 'flats' looks like shoes too, but means apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: Flats are apartments, an example of homes or dwellings.

clue.text: Cricket team to get side out

parts.note: to win something is to get it

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket team aims to dismiss the opposing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side out' sounds like a cricket dismissal but 'out' rearranges SIDE into DIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Windies is the nickname for the West Indies cricket team.

clue.text: See 12
Former clue for IT?

parts.note: the letters I and T are what one, as the Roman numeral, and time, by its abbreviation, would make

explanation.surface: A setter recalls a clue once written for a pair of letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer would clue the letters IT: one gives I and time gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-time champion is a former one, someone who was so once.

clue.text: Smooth limb at end of torso

parts.note: a leg is a limb

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of torso

explanation.surface: A limb attached at the bottom of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction for notes played smoothly, connected without breaks.

clue.text: Angry trade unions striking? It'd be nonsense

indicators.note: angry suggests the letters are stirred up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
these letters are removed from the anagram, with striking meaning taken out

explanation.surface: Furious trade unions on strike would be absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' signals that the letters of IT'D come out of the mixed TRADE UNIONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Unreason is lack of reason or sense, which is nonsense.

clue.text: Another aspect of sex trafficking?

indicators.note: aspect of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question whether another side of the sex trade is being exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, an additional one being another.

clue.text: Escaped fool's head-over-heels

indicators.note: head-over-heels moves the head letter down to the heels, the far end

parts.note: to fool is to delude; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone escaped, a fool tumbling as he ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head-over-heels' moves the D at the front of DELUDE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To have eluded pursuers is to have escaped or evaded them.

clue.text: See 1
Doctor tries to cut back pain and disease

indicators.note: to cut means the anagram piece slices into the reversed word
back means the word for pain is read from right to left

parts.note: to ail is to cause pain or trouble

indicators.note: to doctor something is to alter or tamper with it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician attempts to reduce lower-back pain and illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like part of the phrase back pain but is the reversal signal; 'Doctor' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal, its result going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Listeria is the bacterium behind listeriosis, so the name loosely stands for that illness.

clue.text: A Latin translation for "air pump"

indicators.note: translation suggests the letters are converted into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin rendering is offered for the phrase air pump.
explanation.walkthrough: Antlia, the Air Pump, is a faint southern constellation; the Latin is apt, as constellations have Latin names.
explanation.definitionFit: Antlia is the constellation whose name means the Air Pump.

clue.text: I'm out of guesses — are they cars?

indicators.note: out of means the letters of I'm are dropped from the word for guesses

parts.note: guesses are estimates
I'm gives I and M

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant gives up guessing and asks whether the answer is cars.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an estate car is a station wagon, so estates are cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates is the British term for station wagons, a type of car.

clue.text: Private Eye, say, infiltrates combine

indicators.note: infiltrates means the letter slips inside the word for combine

parts.note: to solder metal parts is to join or combine them

indicators.note: say shows the word eye is meant as heard, giving a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word eye sounds like the letter I

explanation.surface: The satirical magazine Private Eye has an agent working inside a big firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private Eye' reads as the British satirical magazine, but Private is the definition, a rank of soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A private is the lowest rank of soldier in an army.
